title: Glass
author: Ellen Hopkins
current_text: In September 2009, a parent challenged content in Ellen Hopkins’s Glass after noticing an expletive while scanning the book; the challenge led to a review process. Whittier Middle School cancelled Ellen Hopkins’s talk after a parent requested that Glass be removed from the school library.

sources.quote: In September 2009, a challenge to my novel Glass (the sequel to Crank) gave me no other choice. I had donated a school visit to a charity auction, the proceeds of which were to benefit a bookseller who had insurmountable hospital bills.

Except, three days before the planned visit, a parent challenged content in Glass (ostensibly because, while scanning the book, she noticed the f-bomb). So, okay, I understand challenges lead to a review process, as this one did.
We write to protest the recent cancellation of Ellen Hopkins’ talk at Whittier Middle School in response to the request made by one parent to remove Ms. Hopkins’ book, Glass, from the school library.
sources.title: Kids' Right to Read Protests Efforts to Censor Young Adult Author Ellen Hopkins in Oklahoma - National Coalition Against Censorship
